replacements.rationale: Hitchens makes the central distinction easy to recover: atheism does not prescribe one ethical program, since an atheist may be vicious or humanistic, and nonreligious aid can be undertaken for its own sake. The contrast is concrete and its relevance to secular-atrocity parity is apparent. Precision is reduced slightly by the sweeping phrase “anything you like,” the unqualified claim about “most” missionary work, and the compressed reference to humanitarianism’s “slight superiority.”
